title: Range against launch angle
brief:
plots: line with markers, Range (m) against launch angle, for u = 20 m/s, no air resistance
points: 0°, 15°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 75°, 90° give 0.0, 20.4, 35.3, 40.8, 35.3, 20.4, 0.0
html:
<script>
const u = 20, g = 9.8;
const c = Visual.chart({ x: [0, 90], y: [0, 45], xLabel: "Launch angle (°)", yLabel: "Range (m)" });

const data = [[0, 0.0], [15, 20.4], [30, 35.3], [45, 40.8], [60, 35.3], [75, 20.4], [90, 0.0]];
let angle = 0;

// Range on level ground with no air resistance: R = u² sin(2θ) / g
function rangeAt(deg) {
  const th = deg * Math.PI / 180;
  return Math.round(u * u * Math.sin(2 * th) / g * 10) / 10;
}

function draw() {
  c.clear();
  const R = rangeAt(angle);

  // smooth reference curve from the same formula
  c.fn(x => u * u * Math.sin(2 * x * Math.PI / 180) / g, { color: "var(--muted)", dashed: true });

  // the plotted data: line with markers
  c.line(data);
  c.dots(data);

  // selected angle
  c.vline(angle, `${angle}°`);
  c.label(angle, R, `${R.toFixed(1)} m`);

  c.readout([
    `angle = ${angle}°`,
    `range = ${R.toFixed(1)} m`,
    `peak = ${rangeAt(45).toFixed(1)} m at 45°`,
    `u = ${u} m/s, g = ${g} m/s²`
  ]);

  let msg;
  if (angle === 0) {
    msg = "At 0°, the range is 0.0 m, because the ball goes straight along the ground and never comes back up.";
  } else if (angle === 30) {
    msg = "At 30°, the graph shows 35.3 metres.";
  } else if (angle === 45) {
    msg = "At 45°, this is the peak on the graph: 40.8 m, the maximum range for u = 20 m/s.";
  } else {
    msg = `At ${angle}°, the range is ${R.toFixed(1)} m.`;
  }
  Visual.state(msg);
}

Visual.on("angle", v => { angle = v; draw(); });
draw();
</script>
